solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Engagement for management graduate in company time

indicators.note: the graduate sits inside the company-and-time pair, so the word in signals a container

parts.note: an MBA is a Master of Business Administration, a management degree holder

explanation.surface: A business-school graduate's job at a firm is described as a kind of engagement.
explanation.definitionFit: A military engagement is a battle, which is fighting between forces.

clue.text: Conveyance putting competent accountant in credit?

indicators.note: the competent accountant is placed inside the credit abbreviation, signalling a container

parts.note: able means competent
CA is a chartered accountant

explanation.surface: Asking whether a skilled accountant counts a vehicle as a credit.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a cabin hauled up a mountain on a wire, a means of transport.

clue.text: What may provide spark in attraction and love?

parts.note: a magnet is something that attracts
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A question about what gives a romance its spark.
explanation.definitionFit: A small generator produces the spark for ignition in some engines.

clue.text: Other personalities get a loser confused

indicators.note: the letters are muddled up, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: Telling a loser to become confused about other identities.
explanation.definitionFit: A second self, a person's other side, is an alternative personality.

clue.text: Noted writer

parts.note: read not as a famous author but as someone who writes musical notes

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who writes down musical notes is one who creates music.

clue.text: No way would you put flowers here!

definitions.text: No way would you put flowers here!

parts.words: No way would you put flowers here!
parts.note: a refusal phrase meaning 'never while I live', pictured as a grave where flowers go

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is an emphatic refusal; literally, flowers are laid on a corpse.

clue.text: Coppers turn up dead part of flower

parts.note: coppers are pennies, abbreviated P

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: late means dead, as in the late king

explanation.surface: Police officers arrive at a dead body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' suggests police; here they are copper coins, P for pence. 'turn up' makes ETAL from LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Each coloured leaf of a bloom's corolla is one segment of the flower.

clue.text: Instrument from south still in existence

parts.note: extant means surviving, still existing

explanation.surface: A musical instrument from the south that survives.
explanation.definitionFit: A navigator's device for measuring the angle of the sun is a measuring instrument.

clue.text: In a hurry to cast off after game

indicators.note: the cast-off word comes after the game, ordering the pieces

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game
to shed is to cast off

explanation.surface: Someone hurrying to undress after a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Done hastily or in a hurry, as in a hasty job.

clue.text: Disappointment with both taps — keep changing one's mind

parts.note: a blow is a setback or disappointment
a bathroom basin has hot and cold taps

explanation.surface: A frustrating plumbing job with both taps leaves someone dithering.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to vacillate, alternately keen and unenthusiastic.

clue.text: Irrelevant bit of parlour game?

definitions.meaning: a trifle, something of no importance
a table game in which balls are struck into numbered holes

explanation.surface: A trivial piece of some old indoor game.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a mere trifle and a pinball-like table game played indoors.

clue.text: State meals must be taken around ten

indicators.note: the meals are placed around the ten, so this phrase signals a container

parts.note: teas are light afternoon or evening meals in Britain
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A rule that meals must be eaten at about ten o'clock in some state.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the fifty constituent states of the USA, the second largest.

clue.text: Look at bishop argue for viewer protection

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it
B is the chess notation for bishop
to row is to quarrel or argue

explanation.surface: A churchman is told to look at an argument about protecting television viewers.
explanation.definitionFit: The hairy ridge above each eye shields the organ of sight from sweat and rain, the eye being the viewer.

clue.text: Distance from motorway? Three miles cutting out the bend

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first long motorway, read here as MI

indicators.note: the bend is removed from the three miles, so this phrase signals a deletion

parts.note: a league is an old measure of about three miles
a U-bend is a bend shaped like the letter U

explanation.surface: A driver works out a distance from the motorway, three miles once the bend is avoided.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is a London-to-Yorkshire motorway; its 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the number of miles travelled, a measure of distance covered.

clue.text: A wish to get together?

parts.note: to long is to wish or yearn

explanation.surface: Someone hoping for a reunion.
explanation.definitionFit: As in 'bring a friend along', the word means in company with, so together.

clue.text: Wilful but adore changes

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are changed around, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: Someone stubborn whose love nonetheless shifts.
explanation.definitionFit: Stubbornly refusing to change is the wilful obstinacy the word describes.

clue.text: Theatre's type error to be corrected

definitions.note: read as 'Theatre is', the 's linking definition to wordplay

indicators.note: a wrong order of letters to be fixed, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: A typing mistake in a theatre programme awaiting correction.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre company staging a rotating set of plays is a rep company.

clue.text: Element from a metal found in fruit

indicators.note: the metal sits inside the fruit, signalling a container

parts.note: a plum is a fruit
tin is a metal

explanation.surface: A piece of metal discovered in a fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A precious metal, a chemical element with symbol Pt.

clue.text: Dessert mainly otherwise known as main course

indicators.note: most of the dessert word is kept, its final letter dropped

parts.note: a mousse is a light whipped dessert
AKA is the standard abbreviation for also known as

explanation.surface: A menu dish described as mostly dessert but really the main course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' drops the last E of MOUSSE to leave MOUSS.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek baked dish of aubergine and minced lamb, served as an entree.

clue.text: Open mail in military settlement

parts.note: out means open, as in flowers being out
post is mail

explanation.surface: Opening letters at a military base.
explanation.definitionFit: A remote garrison or base of troops is a military settlement.

clue.text: Drums originally featuring in 'Ring Cycle'

indicators.note: the first letter appears inside the ring, signalling a container

parts.note: a peal is a ring of bells

indicators.note: the opening letter of the drums word is taken

explanation.surface: Drums play a part in Wagner's opera cycle of the Ring.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'Ring Cycle' look like Wagner's operas; split, Ring is the fodder and Cycle the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To cycle is to ride a bicycle by pushing with the feet.

clue.text: Party format excludes female submissive type

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: the female letter is left out of format, signalling a deletion

explanation.surface: A party style that bars a meek woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone walked over by others, a weakling, is likened to a mat at the door.

clue.text: Commotion caused by American supporting rear

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below, so comes after

parts.note: the rump is the rear end
US means American

explanation.surface: A row caused by an American backing someone's behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy disturbance or uproar is a commotion.

clue.text: Released around the third of March without a court hearing

indicators.note: the released word goes around the chosen letter, signalling a container

parts.note: untied means set loose, released

indicators.note: the third letter of March is taken

explanation.surface: A prisoner freed around the third of March without ever going before a court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the third of March' looks like a date; it is the letter R, third in MARCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A case never tried in court has not been heard by judges.

clue.text: Golf clubs offering decreases?

definitions.meaning: iron-headed clubs used for approach shots
read as de-creases: pressing with a hot iron removes creases

explanation.surface: Golf clubs that offer price reductions.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal-headed golf clubs, and also flat-irons that smooth out creases in clothes.

clue.text: Confirmed nuisance exposed

parts.note: a bore is a tedious nuisance
out means revealed or exposed

explanation.surface: A confirmed pest is exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confirmed' looks like an adjective (a confirmed bachelor) but is a verb, the past of bear out.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear something out is to corroborate it, and this is its past tense.

clue.text: Post Office impounds stolen print

indicators.note: to impound is to shut in, so the office encloses the stolen goods

parts.note: hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: The Post Office seizes a stolen print.
explanation.definitionFit: A photographic print is a picture produced from a camera image.

clue.text: Handy chap's strange book lots failed to finish

parts.note: odd means strange
Job is a book of the Old Testament

indicators.note: the many word loses its final letter, signalling a deletion

parts.note: many means lots

explanation.surface: A handyman's peculiar book of auction lots that never got completed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lots' looks like auction lots, but it means MANY; 'failed to finish' drops its Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who does small practical repairs around the house is a handy chap.

clue.text: Group developing ideas for land not being used

parts.note: a set is a group

indicators.note: the letters of ideas develop into a new order, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: A team working up ideas for some unused land.
explanation.walkthrough: SET-ASIDE is the EU scheme paying farmers to leave fields fallow.
explanation.definitionFit: Farmland taken out of production under an agricultural scheme lies fallow, unused.

clue.text: Check on cover for safety procedure

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another follows it
the cover of the word safety is its outside letters

parts.note: to stem is to check or stop a flow

explanation.surface: Checking insurance cover as a safety procedure.
explanation.definitionFit: A method or organised way of doing things is a procedure.
